correctness.rationale: The output Bloch radius is at most the largest singular value, giving uniform lower/upper eigenvalue bounds; antipodal singular-vector inputs and the aligned rank-one measurement attain their likelihood-ratio quotient, proving the exact privacy parameter. Local unitaries diagonalize a unital qubit channel to Pauli form, where the normalized Choi state is Bell diagonal and Wootters' formula plus the CP tetrahedron gives concurrence equal to one half of the positive part of the singular-value sum minus one. Privacy bounds every singular value by tanh(epsilon/2), and depolarizing noise saturates all three simultaneously. Fresh checks over 10,000 random Pauli channels matched the singular-value concurrence formula to machine precision and representative depolarizing points saturated the frontier.

The audited positive-branch concurrence optimum therefore requires a new exact privacy parameter for an arbitrary unital Bloch map and a constrained singular-value optimization; no equivalent Resultary record was found.

final_claim: For every unital qubit channel with Bloch singular values s1≥s2≥s3, the optimal pure-QLDP parameter is twice the inverse hyperbolic tangent of s1 and its normalized-Choi concurrence is one half of the positive part of s1+s2+s3−1; consequently the sharp concurrence at privacy budget epsilon is one half of the positive part of 3 tanh(epsilon/2)−1, attained by the depolarizing channel.
limitations: Restricted to unital qubit channels and pure QLDP; no nonunital, higher-dimensional, or positive-delta optimum is asserted.
